## The Problem: Version Control by Hand

You've probably seen a folder like this:
``` 
analysis.R
analysis_v2.R
analysis_final.R
analysis_final_FINAL.R
analysis_final_FINAL_really.R 
```

::: {.incremental}
- You can't remember what changed between versions
- You can't safely delete any of them
- Collaborating means emailing files back and forth
:::

## Git: A Time Machine for Your Project

- Git saves **snapshots** of your work over time, called **commits**
- You can always see what changed, when, and why — and roll back if you
  need to
- Instead of five copies of a file, you keep **one** file with a
  complete history

## Git vs. GitHub

::: {.incremental}
- **Git** — a command-line, distributed version control system. Created
  by Linus Torvalds in 2005. The industry standard.
- **GitHub** — a web/desktop platform *built on* Git, adding a graphical
  interface, cloud hosting, Codespaces, and collaboration tools.
- Git is the engine. GitHub is one (very common) place to park the car.
:::

## Why Version Control Matters for Research

> "A system that records every change to your files, code, and
> documentation over time — creating a complete and auditable history
> of your research workflow."

::: {.incremental}
- Reproducibility
- Collaboration
- Accountability
- A safety net
- Transparency
:::
